哪位联邦法官因贿赂案被众议院弹劾，并由参议院罢免后，三年后竟当选为众议员（正是曾弹劾他的机构）？他在国会服务近30年，并亲自投票参与总统弹劾案？

**提示：**他由吉米·卡特任命，曾作为该州首位黑人联邦法官创造历史，多年后才因贿赂丑闻丧失法袍。

**答案将在下一页揭晓。**

articles.title: Dark Social For Lawyers: How To Track What You Can’t See
articles.content:
“黑暗社交”听起来让人联想到黒暗中的秘密会面，但现实却平淡得多。黑暗社交是指那些旨在个人或小群体之间进行私密交流的数字化通信工具，之所以被称为“黑暗”，并非这些工具或使用方式有什么险恶，而是因为这种活动难以被企业以细节化的方式“看到”，而营销专业人士往往需要这样的数据来为客户制定内容策略。对于律所来说，黑暗社交活动类似于长期以来极为有效的“口碑营销”；然而，通过黑暗社交流量建立的律所声誉却更难以识别。有一些技巧可以帮助敏锐的数字营销专业人士更清晰地了解哪些内容对律所有效、如何有效以及为何有效。

由于律所主要提供的服务类型，大多数客户并不希望向世人公开律师为他们做了什么。同时，许多客户对法律事务的结果感到满意，特别是对律所处理复杂情况的方式感到满意时，会很乐意向朋友或同事推荐同一律所。同样，在社交网络中，朋友或家庭成员常常会帮助彼此，通过查找特定城市中需要法律服务的个人所需的相关法律领域的律师来“跑腿”。

许多这样的推荐和转介会在线上进行，而非面对面或通过语音通话。数字化通信格式，如短信（SMS、MMS、RCS）、电子邮件，甚至工作优化平台如Slack或Microsoft Teams，都能便捷地直接分享律所网站或特定相关页面的链接，因此这些模式在总转介中往往扮演重要角色。然而，这种活动难以以细节化的方式进行追踪。

就像夜视仪能让佩戴者在可见光不足的环境中追踪物体和移动一样，律所和其营销团队也可以使用一些技巧来追踪“黑暗社交”分享的“热信号”。使用一种或几种这样的技巧可以让律所更清楚地了解哪些内容不仅在Google和社交媒体应用中表现良好，而且能引发个人将其分享给他人的真正兴趣。

一些最有效的策略在获取潜在客户的高价值数据时，往往发生在正式接待流程开始之前。虽然在接待流程中应该让接待专家问一个“现场”问题，但也要确保网站上的每一个联系表单都有一个类似“如何知道我们”的问题。

维护一个数据库或电子表格（或其他工具）来追踪答案；理想情况下，你希望有一个选择菜单，带有几个单选按钮或复选框，以及一个如果提供的选项都不符合则提供原创答案的选项。这种“零方数据”收集非常有价值，部分原因是用户自己提供的数据意味着他们已经在某种程度上明确同意你获取该信息。另一个原因是，当你在审查和编目网站访客自己提供的回应时，你不再需要从无面目、无名的点击和流量触发记录中推断。这种间接的、聚合的数据在绘制广泛的模式和趋势方面可能有所帮助，但即使是在最好的情况下，也提供了远远低于来自互联网另一端的人的直接回应的细节化。

如果你的律所已经使用某种链接缩短工具进行社交分享，那么你可能可以使用重定向技术来识别缩短的URL的点击来源，即使网站流量分析显示的数据是通用的“直接”访问。这种策略在比较分析以查看每个平台的总点击数时特别有用。然而，请记住，点击不等于案件；最终，你仍然需要在某处跟踪最终到达你办公室的客户是如何找到你的。

大多数情况下，你可以预计从任何搜索或问答引擎的点击会显示为该来源的转介（例如，“转介来源=Google”或者“转介来源=ChatGPT”）。这意味着，如果你试图确定所有这些“直接”访问的来源，你可以通过创建一个过滤后的分析页面视图来对至少分享类型的推测做出一些有根据的猜测。

排除首页和用于专用、静态内容片段的任何着陆页（例如，你的结果页，或概述一个持续而非限时特别优惠的页面）。剩下的页面，那些具有高度具体主题和关于你实践领域的细节信息的页面，通常要么是搜索引擎转介，要么是“直接”访问。前者显然已经有所统计。后者则通常反映了“黑暗社交”的私人分享活动。

无论访客从何而来，只要他们访问你的网站，这有什么不同？为什么他们首先访问的页面很重要？这些问题的答案是相关的。当我们讨论黑暗社交时，我们不仅仅关注转介来源，就像你可能想到的与Google或AI问答引擎一样。相反，我们真正看到的是一种体验（或从网站流量模式中“绘制”的“形状”），即对体验的估计。

私人分享是个人（成为付费客户的人）认为有价值的内容的强烈指标。与反映人们略过你的网站并决定点击的最常见方式不同，这些黑暗社交分享反映了那些微小的时刻，当有人说，“嘿，我认为这就是你在找的东西”，“觉得你会发现这很有趣”，或“这听起来像是你上周告诉我关于的内容”。这些时刻融入了人际联系和个人意义：我们生活之旅中勾画出的兴趣、担忧和对话。他们留下的指标是一种轨迹标志，这种标志对于技能娴熟的数字营销专家来说，能讲述一个故事。

一旦数据中的模式开始成形，换句话说，一旦故事开始形成某种“叙事”连贯性，你的数字营销专家可能会为你的律所内容策略提供更新的建议。这些新建议并不一定是方向的改变，更不用说表明你的内容做错了什么。律所内容必须从某个地方开始，并创建与潜在客户已知需求和问题相匹配的内容，而你和你的营销团队知道他们可能会有这些问题。

阅读黑暗社交留下的轨迹标志可以为你提供更紧凑的框架。从广撒网（你可能仍然希望在某种程度上这样做），你能够开发出更多与在私人信息中反复分享的内容的结构、主题或专业方法相匹配的内容片段，这样你的律所就有机会融入越来越多的那些时刻，这些时刻发生在大多数分析工具无法跟踪的地方。

你收集和跟踪的所有信息，以及你查看一两次然后再也不使用的所有信息，都永远不会帮助你成长律所。许多数字分析工具的新颖性和显著潜力使人们很容易专注于工具本身的功能，而非工具帮助我们收集的信息所透露的关于律所表现以及到达和遗漏潜在客户的信息。考虑与律所营销团队定期举行会议，不仅审查黑暗社交流量，还要比较其他指标。分析网站结构中各个页面的黑暗社交与已识别转介流量的比例。真正的数字营销专家几乎总是乐于分享他们的见解；与他们分享客户重复提出的问题，并让他们将这些问题与你的网站流量进行匹配，以形成越来越有针对性的内容策略。

安妮特·乔蒂（Annette Choti）拥有20多年的法律经验，是法律会所Law Quill的创始人兼CEO。安妮特撰写了《点击磁石：律所数字营销终极指南》这本畅销书，主持受欢迎的《法律营销休息室》播客，并创建了点击磁石学院，在那里她教授专业人士如何利用强大的LinkedIn平台。作为律师协会、法律协会和营销会议的急需演讲者，安妮特提供了法律营销见解，同时带来了娱乐性的转折。安妮特曾经从事戏剧和专业喜剧，这与法律领域其实并不相隔太远，如果我们都诚实的话。你可以在LinkedIn上找到安妮特，或直接通过电子邮件annette@lawquill.com与她联系。
articles.summary:
“Dark social” can easily conjure images of sinister figures holding clandestine meetings by dead of night. As dramatic as the term sounds, the reality is far more mundane. Dark social is a catchall term for the many digital communication tools that are intended for private conversations between individuals or within small groups, and these socials are “dark” not because there is anything nefarious in the tools or their use but because activity carried out in this way is very difficult for businesses to “see” in the kind of detail that marketing professionals tend to prefer as they develop content strategy for their clients. For law firms, dark social activity tends to mimic the “word of mouth” marketing that has been so invaluable for so long; however, the “reputation” your firm is developing through dark social traffic is much harder to identify. There are a few tricks an astute digital marketing professional may suggest to try and get a sharper picture of what is working for your law firm, how, and why.

Strictly Confidential

Thanks to the kinds of services law firms primarily provide, most clients do not want to broadcast to the world at large exactly what an attorney has done for them. At the same time, in many instances clients who are pleased with the outcomes of their legal matters and especially with the way a particular firm handled a difficult situation will be happy to recommend the same law firm to friends or associates. Similarly, within social networks it is not uncommon for friends or family members to try and help one another out by doing the “leg work” of locating attorneys in relevant practice areas in or near the city where an individual in need of legal services resides.

Many of these recommendations and referrals will take place online, rather than face-to-face or in voice calls. Digital communication formats such as text messaging (SMS, MMS, RCS), email, and even work-optimized platforms such as Slack or Microsoft Teams, facilitate the immediacy of sharing a link directly to a law firm’s website, or even to a specific relevant page, so these modalities often play an important role in total referrals. Activity of this type, however, is difficult to track with any granularity.

Night Vision

Just as night vision goggles allow their wearers to track objects and movements in environments where there is not enough visible light to enable the human eye to discern shapes clearly, there are a few techniques that law firms and their marketing teams can use to trace the “heat signatures” of dark social sharing. Using one or a few of these techniques can make it much easier for your law firm to gain a clear sense of which content is not only performing well on Google and social media apps, but which pieces of content are generating the kind of genuine interest that leads individual human beings to share what they have just found with someone else.

“Zero Party” Data: When Users Tell on Themselves

Often some of the most effective strategies for collecting high-value data from prospective clients comes even before the intake process proper begins. While you should certainly have your intake specialist make a “live” question part of the intake process, make sure that every contact form on your website also asks some version of “How did you hear about us?”

Maintain a database or spreadsheet (or other tool) that tracks the answers; ideally, you would want a selection menu with several radio buttons or checkboxes and an option for providing an original answer if none of the options provided fits. This kind of “zero-party” data collection can be incredibly valuable, in part because the fact that users are giving it to you themselves means they are already, in a sense, explicitly consenting to your access to that information. Another reason the data obtained this way can be especially helpful is that, when you are reviewing and cataloguing responses site visitors provided themselves, you are no longer having to draw inferences from a record of faceless, nameless clicks and traffic triggers. That kind of oblique, aggregated data can be helpful in charting broad patterns and trends, but even at its best it offers significantly less granularity than a direct response from the person at the other end of the internet connection.

Keep It Short ’n’ Sweet

If your law firm already uses any form of link-shortening tool for social sharing, then you may be able to use the redirect technology to identify where the click to the shortened URL originated, even if the data shown in your website’s traffic analytics is a generic “direct” visit. This strategy can be especially useful if you want to run a comparative analysis to see how many total clicks come from each platform. Keep in mind, however, that clicks are not cases; ultimately, you will still need to keep tabs somewhere on how the clients who actually end up in your office are finding you.

Peek Behind the Closed Doors

Most of the time, you can expect a click-through from any search or answer engine to show up as a referral from that source in your traffic analytics (e.g., “referral source = Google,” or “referral source = ChatGPT”). What this means for you, if you are trying to determine where all these “direct” visits are coming from, is that you can often make some educated guesses about at least the type of sharing that brings visitors to your site by creating a filtered view of your analytics page.

Exclude your home page and any landing pages used for specialized, static pieces of content (e.g., your results page, or a page outlining a special offer that operates on an ongoing, rather than limited-time, basis). The pages that are left, the ones with highly specific subjects and granular information about your practice areas, will usually be either those search engine referrals or “direct” visits. The former are obviously accounted for already. The latter, on the other hand, tend to reflect the private sharing of “dark socials” activity.

What To Do With the Information You Collect?

What difference does it make where visitors are coming from, as long as they are visiting your website? Why does it matter which pages they access first? The answers to these questions are related. When we are talking about dark socials, we are looking not just at a referral source, in the way you might think of with Google or one of the AI answer engines. Instead, what we are really seeing (or estimating, from the “shape” drawn from the patterns in site traffic) is an experience.

The Importance of Private Sharing

Private sharing is a strong indication of the content individual human beings (the people who become paying clients) find valuable. Instead of reflecting the most common ways someone skims past your site and decides to click, these dark social shares reflect those tiny moments when someone says, “Hey, I think this is what you were looking for,” or “Thought you’d find this interesting,” or “This sounds like what you were telling me about last week.” Those moments are embedded in human connection and personal significance: the interests and worries and conversations that map out our journey through life. The metrics they leave in their passing are a type of trail sign that, to a skilled digital marketing specialist, tells a story.

Applying Information

Once that story begins to develop some “narrative” coherence, which is to say, “Once a pattern begins to take shape in the data,” your digital marketing specialist will likely have some updated recommendations for your law firm content strategy. These new recommendations are not necessarily a change of direction, much less a sign that your content has been doing anything “wrong.” Law firm content has to start somewhere, and begin by creating pieces of content that align with what your potential clients are known to need and the questions you and your marketing team know they are likely to have.

What reading the trail sign left by dark socials can do for you is tighten the frame. From casting a wide net (which you may still want to do on some level), you are able to develop more pieces of content that line up with the structure or subject matter or professional approach seen in the content that repeatedly gets shared in personal messages, so that your law firm has a chance to become embedded in more and more of those moments that take place where most analytics tools cannot follow.

Keep Your Ear to the Ground

None of the information you collect and track, and none of the information you view in a spreadsheet once or twice and then never use, will ever help you grow your law firm. The novelty and the impressive potential of many digital analytics tools can make it easy to become focused on the function of the tools themselves, rather than on what the information they have helped us gather has to say about your law firm’s performance and where it is reaching, and missing, potential clients. Consider setting up a regular schedule of meetings with your law firm marketing team to review not just dark social traffic, but other metrics to which it might compare. Examine the ratio of dark social to identified referral traffic on individual pages within your site structure. True experts in digital marketing are almost always happy to be asked for their insights; share with them the repeated questions you get from clients and let them match those questions against your site traffic to inform an increasingly targeted content strategy.

Annette Choti, Esq., has over two decades of legal experience and is the Founder & CEO of Law Quill, a concierge legal marketing agency for law firms.  Annette authored the bestselling book Click Magnet: The Ultimate Guide To Digital Marketing For Law Firms, hosts the popular Legal Marketing Lounge podcast, and founded Click Magnet Academy where she teaches professionals to leverage the powerful LinkedIn platform. As a sought after speaker for Bar Associations, Legal Associations, and Marketing Conferences, Annette provides legal marketing insight along with an entertaining twist. Annette used to do theatre and professional comedy, which is not so different from the legal field if we are all being honest. Annette can be found on LinkedIn or directly through email at Annette@LawQuill.com 

The post Dark Social For Lawyers: How To Track What You Can’t See appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Lawyers Should Think Twice Before CCing Bosses To An Email
articles.content:
在法律行业中，电子邮件是律师与同事、对手、客户及其他从业者沟通的最重要方式之一。大多数律师在典型的工作日中可能会发送数十甚至数百封邮件。由于电子邮件使用频率极高，律师可能不会对抄送收件人多加思考。然而，将某人添加到邮件串中有时会传递出其他信息，律师在不必要地抄送上级或与会话无关的人时应慎重考虑。

在职业早期，我曾遇到过一些情况，有人会抄送上级，似乎是对谈话进展不满意。也许他们没有得到预期的回复速度，或者对某些内容有异议。与其继续沟通，不如将上级或更高级别的人添加到邮件串中。这种行为几乎总是会立即改变讨论的语气。

抄送某人的上级可能被视为一种升级。实际上，人们联系上级的主要原因之一是对下属处理情况不满意。任何与客户服务打过交道的人都应该理解这一点。要求与经理交谈通常被视为幼稚的行为，通常意味着客户认为出了问题，并希望更高权限的人介入。

同样的暗示也存在于专业邮件中。如果两名律师一直在讨论常规问题，其中一人突然抄送另一名律师的上级，明显的问题是为什么需要将上级拉进讨论。即使发送者并无意抱怨另一名律师，收件人也可能合理地认为发送者试图施加压力或暗示收件人处理不当。

这在法律行业尤其有害，因为关系至关重要。律师经常需要从对手和同事那里争取便利。律师会请求延期、调整时间安排、调查上的便利，以及无数其他专业上的照顾。如果某人认为另一名律师在上级面前不必要地使其难堪，那么未来可能会更不愿意提供便利。

不必要的抄送还可能破坏工作场所内的关系。假设一名律师正在与外部人士讨论常规问题，对方突然抄送了负责监督该律师的合伙人。合伙人可能会怀疑是否出现了需要关注的问题。律师可能需要解释情况，尽管实际上并没有发生任何特殊情况。最初的简单邮件交流现在可能为数人带来了压力和额外的工作。

当然，有许多情况需要抄送上级是完全合适的。如果某人已经参与了某事，他们显然应该被包含在相关的沟通中。同样，如果问题经过合理的努力后仍未解决，涉及有额外权限的人可能是必要的。律师不应仅因为该人是更高级别而避免抄送。

但是，在保持相关人士知情与利用抄送行作为筹码之间存在着显著的区别。律师有时会抄送他人，因为他们认为这样可以使收件人更快地回应或更认真地对待请求。这种策略可能在短期内有效，但可能带来巨大的际关系代价。没有人喜欢感觉有人不必要地越过自己的头顶。

此外，抄送更多人可能会使解决分歧变得更加困难。一个人可能愿意在私下交流中妥协或承认错误。一旦上级、客户或其他律师加入对话，人们可能会变得更加防备。突然之间，每个人都有一个观众，原本可以缓和的立场变得更难以放弃，而不必担心妥协会带来什么影响。

在添加某人的上级到邮件之前，律师应自问一个简单的问题：这个人真的需要参与吗？如果答案是肯定的，通常没有问题。但如果真正的原因是增加压力、表达不满或确保某人知道上级在监督，那么最好先直接继续沟通。

律师已经处理了足够的不必要冲突。我们不应通过简单的邮件抄送行增加摩擦。在许多情况下，直接与某人沟通而非立即涉及其上级表明了专业尊重。而保持这种尊重可能比通过不必要抄送上级带来的短期优势更有价值。

乔丹·罗斯曼（Jordan Rothman）是罗斯曼律师事务所（The Rothman Law Firm）的合伙人，该事务所是一家全方位服务的纽约和新泽西律师事务所。他还是学生债务日志（Student Debt Diaries）的创始人，该网站讨论了他如何偿还学生贷款。您可以通过电子邮件jordan@rothman.law联系乔丹。
articles.summary:
Email is one of the most important ways lawyers communicate with colleagues, adversaries, clients, and pretty much everyone else involved in the legal profession. Most lawyers probably send dozens, if not hundreds, of emails during a typical workday. Because email is so ubiquitous, lawyers might not put much thought into whom they copy on a message. However, adding someone to an email chain can sometimes send a message of its own, and lawyers should think twice before unnecessarily copying superiors or other people who have no reason to be involved in a conversation.

Earlier in my career, I sometimes encountered situations in which someone would copy a superior on an email seemingly because they were dissatisfied with how a conversation was progressing. Perhaps they did not receive a response as quickly as they wanted, or perhaps they disagreed with something that had been said. Rather than simply continuing the conversation, the person added a boss or another higher-ranking individual to the email chain. This almost always changed the tone of the discussion immediately.

Copying someone’s boss on an email can easily be interpreted as an escalation. Indeed, one of the main reasons people contact a superior is because they are dissatisfied with how a subordinate handled a situation. Anyone who has ever dealt with customer service probably understands this dynamic. Asking to speak with a manager is often seen as petty behavior, and usually means that the customer believes something has gone wrong and wants someone with more authority to intervene.

The same implication can exist in professional emails. If two lawyers have been communicating about a routine issue and one suddenly copies the other lawyer’s boss, the obvious question is why the superior needed to be brought into the discussion. Even if the sender did not intend to complain about the other lawyer, the recipient may reasonably believe that the sender is trying to apply pressure or suggest that the recipient has somehow mishandled the situation.

This can be particularly damaging in the legal profession because relationships matter. Lawyers routinely need favors from adversaries and colleagues. Attorneys request extensions, scheduling accommodations, discovery courtesies, and countless other professional considerations. Someone who feels that another lawyer unnecessarily tried to embarrass them in front of a boss may understandably be less enthusiastic about extending courtesies in the future.

Unnecessary CCs can also undermine relationships within a workplace. Suppose an associate is discussing a routine issue with someone outside the firm and that person suddenly copies a partner supervising the associate. The partner may wonder whether there is a problem that requires attention. The associate may then need to explain the situation even though nothing unusual happened in the first place. A simple email exchange has now potentially created stress and additional work for several people.

Of course, there are plenty of situations in which copying a superior is entirely appropriate. If someone is already involved in a matter, they should obviously be included on relevant communications. Similarly, if an issue genuinely needs to be escalated after reasonable efforts to resolve it have failed, involving someone with additional authority may be necessary. Lawyers should not avoid copying someone merely because that person happens to be more senior.

But there is a meaningful difference between keeping relevant people informed and using the CC line as leverage. Lawyers sometimes copy people because they believe doing so will make the recipient respond faster or take a request more seriously. That tactic might work in the short term, but it can come with a substantial interpersonal cost. Nobody enjoys feeling as though someone went over their head unnecessarily.

Moreover, copying additional people can make resolving a disagreement more difficult. A person might be willing to compromise or acknowledge a mistake during a private exchange. Once supervisors, clients, or other lawyers are watching the conversation, however, people can become more defensive. Suddenly, everyone has an audience, and positions that could have been softened become harder to abandon without someone worrying about how the concession will look.

Before adding someone’s superior to an email, lawyers should therefore ask themselves a simple question: does this person actually need to be involved? If the answer is yes, there is usually nothing wrong with copying them. But if the real reason is to increase pressure, express displeasure, or make sure someone knows that their boss is watching, it may be better to continue the conversation directly first.

Lawyers already deal with enough unnecessary conflict. We should not create additional friction through something as simple as the CC line of an email. In many circumstances, communicating directly with someone rather than immediately involving their superior demonstrates professional respect. And preserving that respect can be far more valuable than whatever short-term advantage might come from unnecessarily copying the boss.

Jordan Rothman is a partner of The Rothman Law Firm, a full-service New York and New Jersey law firm. He is also the founder of Student Debt Diaries, a website discussing how he paid off his student loans. You can reach Jordan through email at jordan@rothman.law.

The post Lawyers Should Think Twice Before CCing Bosses To An Email appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: ABA Plans Major Restructuring Amid Financial Struggles
articles.content:
编辑注：欢迎收看我们的每日专栏《每日金句》。

这是一项重大任务，因为我们已经有40或50年没有重新审视组织结构了。我们需要进入21世纪。
——美国律师协会（ABA）主席巴巴拉·霍华德（Barbara Howard）在接受Bloomberg Law采访时表示，谈及该组织的潜在重组计划，可能包括合并委员会和小组，以应对收入下滑的财政困境。ABA预计在本财年末（本月）收入将有所下降，且支出已超收入。

斯塔西·扎雷茨基（Staci Zaretsky）是《法律之上》的执行编辑，自2011年起一直担任该职务。她很希望听到您的声音，欢迎发送电子邮件给她，提供任何线索、问题、评论或批评。您可以在Bluesky、X/Twitter和Threads上关注她，或在LinkedIn上与她联系。

articles.summary:
Ed. note: Welcome to our daily feature, Quote of the Day.

That’s a big undertaking because we haven’t looked at renovating how we are structured for 40 or 50 years. We need to move into the 21st century.

— Barbara Howard, president of the American Bar Association, in comments given to Bloomberg Law, concerning the organization’s prospective restructuring, which could include combining committees and panels as the ABA looks to rein in spending amid declining revenue. The ABA is on track to see its revenue dip when its fiscal year ends later this month, and has already spent more than it has taken in.

Staci Zaretsky is the managing editor of Above the Law, where she’s worked since 2011. She’d love to hear from you, so please feel free to email her with any tips, questions, comments, or critiques. You can follow her on Bluesky, X/Twitter, and Threads, or connect with her on LinkedIn.
